article.Citation/Title: Vanderijst, L., Hever, F., Buot, A., Daure, C., Benoit, J., Hanak, C., Veeser, J., Morgieve, M., Campanella, S., Kornreich, C., Mallet, L., Leys, C., & Noel, X. (2024). Psilocybin-assisted therapy for severe alcohol use disorder: protocol for a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, 7-month parallel-group phase II superiority trial. BMC Psychiatry, 24, 77.
article.EligibilityNote: Labeled a study protocol; no participants had been enrolled, screened, or dosed at publication, so no intervention was administered (fails criterion a) and no substance-use outcome data are reported anywhere in the article (fails criterion b).
article.InterventionDescription: Psilocybin single oral dose: 30 mg (high dose) vs 5 mg (active placebo), embedded in ACT-based psychotherapy (2 preparation, 1 dosing, 2 integration sessions) during 4-week inpatient alcohol detoxification.

article.Outcome: This is a study protocol (BMC Psychiatry, 2024, DOI s12888-024-05502-y). At the time of publication no participants had been enrolled or dosed; the article describes the planned primary clinical outcome (between-group change in % heavy drinking days, baseline to 4 weeks posthospital discharge, Methods 'Primary clinical outcome') but reports no observed effect size anywhere in the text. Coded '.'.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic is reported; the Data analysis section names the planned statistical models (mixed-model ANOVA with Helmert contrasts, GLMM, mediation analyses) but presents no computed values. Coded '.'.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: The protocol specifies a planned total N=62 (31 high-dose/31 active-placebo, powered for 46 completers assuming 25% attrition; Methods 'Sample size'), but this is a target enrollment figure, not a final analyzed N from a completed analysis of Outcome. No analysis has occurred, so coded '.' rather than substituting the planned N.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: All fourteen elements are addressed except 'results': as a protocol, the article has no results section and reports no outcome data (not even 'no results yet' language qualifies as describing results). Every other element is described in detail: objective/hypotheses (Background/Proposed study), design (double-blind RCT, 7-month parallel-group phase II), setting (Brugmann University Hospital Psychiatry Dept, inpatient detox unit), eligibility (explicit inclusion/exclusion lists), intervention (30mg psilocybin + ACT-based psychotherapy), comparator (5mg active placebo, rationale given), outcomes (primary/secondary/exploratory all itemized with instruments, Table 1), sample size/power (a priori power calc, Cohen's f=0.25, power=0.9), randomization (computer-generated, 1:1), blinding (double-blind, blinding-efficacy assessment plan), statistical methods (Data analysis section), harms (AE classification by severity/causality/expectedness, safety as a co-primary outcome), and funding/COI (Funding and Competing interests sections). n_met=13/14 meets the >=13 threshold, so the binary is 1.

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 3 (cannot be determined) because no outcome data of any kind are reported; directionality of any treatment effect is genuinely unknown/unassessed, not merely absent as in a null single-arm result.
article.Clincial Trial YN: Coded 0 to avoid contradicting the eligibility screen. Criterion (a) failed because the article does not report a conducted clinical trial: no participant has been enrolled, randomized, or dosed, and no prospective outcome assessment has occurred. The protocol describes a planned RCT design, but per the prompt's contradiction rule, Clincial Trial YN=1 alongside a failed criterion (a) is disallowed.
article.RandomizationYN: Coded 1 from the described design ('computer-generated randomization', 1:1 allocation, Methods) even though Clincial Trial YN=0, per instruction that design features the protocol specifies may still be coded from the described design despite the trial not having been executed/reported.
article.BlindingYN: Coded 1: the protocol specifies a double-blind design with systematic blinding-efficacy assessment (participants and therapists asked to guess allocation) — a specified design feature, not an executed/reported result.
article.Double+Blind: Coded 1, matching BlindingYN=1: the title and Methods explicitly specify 'double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled' design.
article.Comparator: Coded 1: active placebo condition (5mg psilocybin, a low-dose comparator) is specified; this is a dose-comparison design, which counts as 1 per the field rule. Comparator's nature: low (5mg) vs high (30mg) dose of the same substance, chosen to maintain blinding while remaining sub-therapeutic (Explanation for choice of comparator section).
article.Retention (%): Not calculable: zero participants have been enrolled or completed the study at the time of this protocol's publication, so no completers/denominator counts exist. Coded '.' (distinct from the design-specified fields above, since retention is an empirical outcome, not a design parameter).
article.Age_Median: The article gives only the eligibility age range (21-64 years) as an inclusion criterion, not the median/mean age of an actual enrolled sample (none exists yet). Since the field requires the bracket containing the sample's actual median/mean age, coded '.' rather than inferring a bracket from the eligibility bound.
article.PercentFem: Not reported; no participants have been enrolled. Coded '.'.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Not reported; no participants have been enrolled and no demographic data exist yet. Coded '.'.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Trial conducted at Brugmann University Hospital, Brussels, Belgium (monocentric). Coded 'NonUS'.
article.Followup in months: Coded 6, the longest follow-up timepoint specified in the protocol's schedule (Table 1: 6-month posthospital-discharge follow-up for heavy drinking, drinking days, abstinence, mood, anxiety, trauma, global functioning). This is the protocol-specified follow-up horizon, not an observed/reported follow-up outcome, since no participant has yet reached this timepoint.
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 1: the protocol specifies safety as a co-primary outcome, with AEs 'systematically recorded at each study visit and follow-up' and classified by severity, causality, and expectedness (Primary feasibility and safety outcomes section; Table 1 tracks 'Adverse events' at nearly every visit). This reflects the specified assessment plan, consistent with SafetyReported='Y' below.
article.SafetyReported: Coded 'Y' on the basis that an explicit Safety/Adverse Events assessment plan and section exist in the article (per the field's judging criterion: 'whether an Adverse Events/Safety section... exists'), even though the trial has not yet been conducted and so no AE data exist. This is a genuinely ambiguous case not covered by the three-state table in the prompt (which assumes a completed study); flagged here rather than buried. The alternative reading (SafetyReported='N' because nothing has actually been assessed yet) was considered but rejected because the article unambiguously commits to and describes a systematic AE-assessment methodology, unlike a true 'authors never looked' case.
article.AnyAEReported: Coded 'N': zero AEs have occurred or been reported because the trial has not yet dosed any participant. This differs from the classic 'no AEs occurred' scenario (which implies a completed safety assessment with a true negative finding) but produces the same downstream coding; flagged as a judgment call.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Coded 0, consistent with AnyAEReported='N' per the three-state convention (0 only permitted when AnyAEReported='N').
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Coded 0: zero participants have been dosed, so zero participants can have an AE to date.
article.AE_denominator: Coded '.': no safety population has been assessed yet (zero participants dosed), so no denominator exists. Distinguished from the 'SafetyReported=N' case, where '.' is also used but for a different reason (no assessment planned at all); here the plan exists but has not yet been executed on any participant.
article.ArmScope: Coded 'NA': with zero participants dosed in either arm, arm scope for AE reporting genuinely does not apply yet (not merely because the study has one arm — it currently has zero exposed participants of any kind).
article.WorstSeverity: Coded 'None', consistent with AnyAEReported='N' per the three-state convention.
article.BaseStatus: Coded 'Severe': inclusion criteria require a DSM-5-TR diagnosis of severe alcohol use disorder (6 or more criteria), explicitly stated in both Background ('sAUD') and inclusion criteria.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: Coded 1: the secondary hypotheses explicitly state the high-dose group is expected to show 'a greater improvement in health-related quality of life compared to the active placebo group' (Background/Proposed study, secondary hypotheses), and Table 1 tracks 'Global functioning' as a planned outcome.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 1: recruitment is planned from the routine inpatient alcohol-detoxification pathway at a public university hospital (real-world clinical population), explicitly framed by the authors as 'pragmatic' (Background: 'trials that are more pragmatic in nature'; Recruitment section). Flagged as non-obvious because the Discussion itself notes this pragmatic aim is constrained by 'strict and rather restrictive inclusion and exclusion criteria', which somewhat limits representativeness.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 1: the primary and secondary clinical outcomes (percentage of heavy drinking days, percentage of days of abstinence, drinks per day, tracked from baseline through 4 weeks and 6 months posthospital discharge) function as a return-to-use/relapse measure, though the article does not use the word 'relapse' as a named instrument; treated as functionally equivalent tracking of return to problematic drinking after detoxification.
article.SchemaRevisionNote: 2026-09-03 schema-revision splice: ConfoundYN/PVal removed, MediatingYN/ModeratingYN/HypothesisTestReportedYN added, sourced from a separate v3 extraction run (PromptVersion v1.3) rather than this file's own v1.2 run. Every other field in this file is unchanged from the original v1.2 extraction -- this file is now a hybrid of two runs for these 3 fields only. See clinical_adjudication.md '2026-09-03 -- Coding-scheme revision' for the full rationale.

config_proposal.metric: No statistic reported (trial protocol; no participants dosed, no outcome data collected)
config_proposal.note: This is a trial protocol (registered EudraCT 2022-002369-14 / NCT06160232, recruitment starting winter 2024, expected completion autumn 2026). No participants have been dosed and no outcome data of any kind exist, so no effect-size conversion is defensible. Excluded from Tier 1 pending publication of the trial's actual results.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Study protocol with zero reported outcome data; there is nothing to classify qualitatively, positively or negatively, until results are published.
